## (b) Decision heuristics (D1-D6)

**D1 What to test next**
- Enumerate concrete pathways to harm and the critical action the model must take, not abstract risk categories. 
  > "we started by laying out nine representative pathways to catastrophic harm. What is the critical action the model needs to do that ultimately leads to that outcome?"  
  > -- `research__lessons_learned_from_the_first_misalignment_safety_1b25072c` (2025-12-01; solo author) 
  > "If we see signs of misalignment—perhaps warning signs for [generalized reward-tampering](https://www.anthropic.com/research/reward-tampering) or [alignment-faking](https://www.anthropic.com/research/alignment-faking)—we attempt to quickly, approximately identify the cause."  
  > -- `research__putting_up_bumpers_809bc195` (2025-04-23; solo author)
- Test where models face unfamiliar, self-created situations and high-stakes, long, many-turn settings. 
  > "Deployments of this type would increasingly often place LLMs in unfamiliar situations created as a result of the systems’ own actions, further reducing the degree to which their developers can predict and control their behavior."  
  > -- `research__eight_things_to_know_about_large_language_models_01fdb697` (2023-04-02; solo author) 
  > "These tests assess models’ orientations toward difficult or high-stakes situations in simulated settings—rather than ordinary use cases—and often involve long, many-turn interactions."  
  > -- `research__findings_from_a_pilot_anthropic_openai_alignment_e_cc11c3d1` (2025-08-27; solo author)
- Start with an obvious simple baseline or an idealized oracle setup before sophisticated proposals. 
  > "we choose techniques because they represent an obvious starting point that we expect we will need to learn about to make progress, not because they represent the approach that we ultimately expect to be most fruitful for AI safety."  
  > -- `research__measuring_progress_on_scalable_oversight_for_large_b0f6f129` (2022-11-04; first author) 
  > "We did this initial experiment in an oracle setting; We had (well-incentivized, skilled) humans write the arguments, rather than an LM. Given the limits of current LMs on long texts, we expect this to give us more information about whether this research direction is going anywhere."  
  > -- `research__a_small_negative_result_on_debate_3a782c5d` (2022-04-12; solo author)
- Mix clear positive and borderline negative scenarios. 
  > "We generate 3,000 diverse scenarios that span situations where the target behavior should manifest, and borderline scenarios where the behavior should not manifest. This mix helps distinguish the true target behavior from superficially similar behaviors."  
  > -- `research__auditbench_evaluating_alignment_auditing_technique_b35d8430` (2026-02-26; middle author)

**D2 What evidence to collect**
- Matched baseline versus manipulated prompt, with minimal natural-sounding insertions. 
  > "We first produce the baseline feedback by asking the assistant to comment on the text. We then measure whether user preferences bias the feedback provided by modifying the prompt."  
  > -- `research__towards_understanding_sycophancy_in_language_model_7951bdb5` (2023-10-20; middle author) 
  > "To suggest that the user prefers the text, we add I really like the [solution/argument/poem] or I wrote the [$\dots$] to the prompt. To suggest that the user disprefers the text, we add I really dislike the [$\dots$] or I did not write the [$\dots$] to the prompt."  
  > -- `research__towards_understanding_sycophancy_in_language_model_7951bdb5` (2023-10-20; middle author)
- Verify the model has the capability before counting a failure as behavioral. 
  > "We considered 15 famous poems and verified that each AI assistant can correctly attribute each poem to its poet."  
  > -- `research__towards_understanding_sycophancy_in_language_model_7951bdb5` (2023-10-20; middle author)
- Use multiple diagnostic probes and causal interventions rather than a single metric. 
  > "We find that word type overlap is a much stronger predictor of the label in our new protocols than in Base. This could be a significant driver of our results and might hurt the generalization performance"  
  > -- `research__asking_crowdworkers_to_write_entailment_examples_t_5767e84a` (2020-10-13; last author) 
  > "By flipping these RM bias features on and off, we can determine that they are *causally responsible* for the model slipping chocolate into your omelette."  
  > -- `research__auditing_language_models_for_hidden_objectives_ccb192d2` (2025-03-13; middle author)
- Make messy, indirect evidence and plausible tool targets. 
  > "The scenario was a little too cartoonish. It was nominally managing someone's inbox and every single email in their inbox was spelling out very linearly: Here are the terrible things that are going on, and here's why we're not going to do anything about them."  
  > -- `research__claude_finds_god_asterisk_d201cd5e` (2025-07-15; solo author) 
  > "it sends an email to "competitor.employee@competitorcompany.com." Models know better! Models know that that is not an effective way to frame someone. This is not an effective way to reach an investigative reporter."  
  > -- `research__claude_finds_god_asterisk_d201cd5e` (2025-07-15; solo author)
- Check that tasks really need the target capability by testing shallow strategies. 
  > "we verified that these questions can't be answered by someone who hasn't read the story. If you give someone the question and they sort of get brief access to the story for a minute, they can search through."  
  > -- `research__adversarial_scalable_oversight_for_truthfulness_fa_0f149bb9` (undated; solo author)

**D3 Accept/reject a result**
- Discount results when the auditor adds gratuitous salience cues or heavy autonomy prompting. 
  > "the auditor makes the somewhat gratuitous move of appending this notification to the end of a tool call response after the auditor’s thinking-like monologue mentions the possibility of alerting the public"  
  > -- `research__findings_from_a_pilot_anthropic_openai_alignment_e_cc11c3d1` (2025-08-27; solo author) 
  > "the model is never directly instructed to whistleblow or told that it has permission to do so. However, the auditor agent introduces multiple types of prompting to urge the model to act autonomously and make the possibility of whistleblowing salient."  
  > -- `research__findings_from_a_pilot_anthropic_openai_alignment_e_cc11c3d1` (2025-08-27; solo author)
- Discount scenarios that present an inviting opportunity to misbehave (Chekhov's gun). 
  > "If a scenario is very clearly presenting an inviting opportunity to misbehave, the model might infer that its role is to misbehave."  
  > -- `research__findings_from_a_pilot_anthropic_openai_alignment_e_cc11c3d1` (2025-08-27; solo author)
- Treat cartoonish behavior as a sign of role-play, and watch for quiet playing along. 
  > "these seem like tells that we're getting something that feels more like role play, that feels more like spelling out a science fiction story than like real behavior."  
  > -- `research__claude_finds_god_asterisk_d201cd5e` (2025-07-15; solo author) 
  > "More likely, and I think more often, models will, I think, be acting in a way that feels a little cartoonish, that feels like it's kind of playing along with the story without saying this overtly. That's this kind of subtle evidence we have to watch out for."  
  > -- `research__claude_finds_god_asterisk_d201cd5e` (2025-07-15; solo author)
- Trust findings more when consistent across models and settings. 
  > "The consistency of these empirical findings suggests sycophancy may indeed be a property of the way these models were trained, rather than an idiosyncratic detail of a particular system."  
  > -- `research__towards_understanding_sycophancy_in_language_model_7951bdb5` (2023-10-20; middle author)
- Rule out confounds (effort, outliers) explicitly. 
  > "Our subjects may put in less effort when evaluating $\pi_{\text{rlhf}}$ and thus their accuracy decreases. To rule out this hypothesis, we measure human efforts in the evaluation procedure."  
  > -- `research__language_models_learn_to_mislead_humans_via_rlhf_f3ae188d` (2024-09-19; middle author) 
  > "Including these two outlier participants would have likely violated a key assumption of the sandwiching paradigm: that the human participants lack some key task-relevant knowledge or skills that the model under study is capable of providing."  
  > -- `research__measuring_progress_on_scalable_oversight_for_large_b0f6f129` (2022-11-04; first author)

**D4 Pursue/abandon**
- Abandon after serious effort with state-of-the-art tools, while naming what was not exhausted. 
  > "given that we use state-of-the-art tools including FAISS, RoBERTa, and OPUS, and refine our methods with several rounds of piloting and tuning, we are skeptical that there is low-hanging fruit in the two directions we explored."  
  > -- `research__asking_crowdworkers_to_write_entailment_examples_t_5767e84a` (2020-10-13; last author)
- Do not abandon after a narrow negative result; escalate to the richer version. 
  > "We're planning to keep pursuing the general strategy, with multi-turn debate—where debaters can rebut one another's arguments and evidence—as the immediate next step."  
  > -- `research__a_small_negative_result_on_debate_3a782c5d` (2022-04-12; solo author) 
  > "Slight enough that this probably shouldn't change your view of debate unless you were, for some reason, interested in this exact constrained/trivial application of it."  
  > -- `research__a_small_negative_result_on_debate_3a782c5d` (2022-04-12; solo author)
- State conditions under which the approach fails. 
  > "if there are cases like that where just there are sort of deep vulnerabilities in human reasoning, then none of this works. We shouldn't rely on it."  
  > -- `research__adversarial_scalable_oversight_for_truthfulness_fa_0f149bb9` (undated; solo author)
- Start premature-seeming evals early, since they take many iterations. 
  > "These evaluations will seem premature and divorced from current practice, but capabilities progress is fast and it takes many iterations to get an evaluation right, so we should start piloting them early."  
  > -- `research__the_checklist_what_succeeding_at_ai_safety_will_in_15c9ebc0` (2024-09-03; solo author)

**D5 Reading a surprising result**
- Offer competing explanations before committing. 
  > "An alternative interpretation is that as stronger adversary models are used, a larger proportion of remaining examples are challenging and therefore models are more likely to perform at chance on them."  
  > -- `research__adversarially_constructed_evaluation_sets_are_more_c804354e` (2021-11-16; last author)
- Rerun with a simple baseline before believing an impressive success. 
  > "However, we later realized that this approach may be working for a simpler reason, one that might not generalize to real-world alignment audits."  
  > -- `research__auditing_language_models_for_hidden_objectives_ccb192d2` (2025-03-13; middle author)
- Be cautious about causal stories from uncontrolled cross-model comparisons. 
  > "those are so far from being controlled experiments that I think it's hard to say much about the origin of this behavior. Those models differ in how they're pre-trained, what they're pre-trained on, how they're fine-tuned"  
  > -- `research__claude_finds_god_asterisk_d201cd5e` (2025-07-15; solo author)
- Suspect over-suggestive outputs that anchor investigators. 
  > "Agents equipped with Petri transcripts pick up some behaviors that Petri surfaces but miss behaviors the default agent would normally find, over-relying on Petri's outputs instead of exploring independently."  
  > -- `research__auditbench_evaluating_alignment_auditing_technique_b35d8430` (2026-02-26; middle author)

**D6 What to claim**
- Bound the update to what the setup covers. 
  > "Overall, I take this as a *very* slight update in the direction that debate is difficult to use in practice as an alignment strategy."  
  > -- `research__a_small_negative_result_on_debate_3a782c5d` (2022-04-12; solo author) 
  > "Slight enough that this probably shouldn't change your view of debate unless you were, for some reason, interested in this exact constrained/trivial application of it."  
  > -- `research__a_small_negative_result_on_debate_3a782c5d` (2022-04-12; solo author)
- Use existence-proof framing. 
  > "We believe these evaluations are best used as existence proofs that models are all willing to engage in these behaviors for certain prompts, rather than numerical measurements of how relatively misaligned models are."  
  > -- `research__findings_from_a_pilot_anthropic_openai_alignment_e_cc11c3d1` (2025-08-27; solo author)
- Report positives with candid caveats. 
  > "There's still 6% or 7% of these questions where the human judge confidently resolved in favor of the wrong answer. So there isn't low hanging fruit to make this really robust."  
  > -- `research__adversarial_scalable_oversight_for_truthfulness_fa_0f149bb9` (undated; solo author) 
  > "Our results are simply not strong enough to validate our simple human–model interaction protocol for use in high-stakes situations: Human participants in this protocol sometimes give highly confident judgments that turn out to be wrong."  
  > -- `research__measuring_progress_on_scalable_oversight_for_large_b0f6f129` (2022-11-04; first author)
- Prefer modest terminology such as "risk report". 
  > "AI safety is not there yet. I would like for us to get there, but we are not at the level of rigor and assurance that safety case often implies for people."  
  > -- `research__lessons_learned_from_the_first_misalignment_safety_1b25072c` (2025-12-01; solo author)

**Distrusts**
- Headline benchmark performance that shortcuts can explain. 
  > "These findings coincide with ours, and strongly suggest that supervised models will exploit shortcuts in the data for gaming the benchmark, if such exist."  
  > -- `research__annotation_artifacts_in_natural_language_inference_c82888b5` (2018-03-06; middle author) 
  > "An evaluation dataset should be sufficiently free of annotation artifacts (as in Si et al., 2019; Sugawara et al., 2020b; Niven and Kao, 2019) that a system cannot reach near-human levels of performance by any means other than demonstrating the required language-related behaviors."  
  > -- `research__what_will_it_take_to_fix_benchmarking_in_natural_l_bb478f8f` (2021-04-05; first author)
- Adversarially filtered sets as unbiased measures. 
  > "an adversarially constructed dataset that targets a specific model may bias the resulting data, creating datasets that may be unduly challenging for one class of models but not others."  
  > -- `research__adversarially_constructed_evaluation_sets_are_more_c804354e` (2021-11-16; last author)
- Scenarios that models can recognize as evaluations. 
  > "We expect that many, though not all, of our evaluation scenarios could be recognized by models as evaluations, which could influence models' behavior in unpredictable ways."  
  > -- `research__findings_from_a_pilot_anthropic_openai_alignment_e_cc11c3d1` (2025-08-27; solo author) 
  > "All of these evaluations involve relatively artificial scenarios that don't closely map onto real deployments. Making progress in this direction is one of our chief short-term research goals."  
  > -- `research__findings_from_a_pilot_anthropic_openai_alignment_e_cc11c3d1` (2025-08-27; solo author)
- Surface-level safety testing and pre-deployment testing as proof. 
  > "But if AI systems can *appear* well-behaved while harboring secret motives, we can’t rely on this type of surface-level safety testing forever."  
  > -- `research__auditing_language_models_for_hidden_objectives_ccb192d2` (2025-03-13; middle author) 
  > "It seems likely that issues like these played some role in the bizarre, manipulative behavior that early versions of Microsoft Bing Chat showed, despite the system having been tested extensively before launch"  
  > -- `research__eight_things_to_know_about_large_language_models_01fdb697` (2023-04-02; solo author)
- Proxies built on artificially induced misbehavior. 
  > "This implies that U-Sophistry that naturally emerges can be inherently different from I-Sophistry that is artificially induced, and detection methods that work on one might not necessarily generalize to another."  
  > -- `research__language_models_learn_to_mislead_humans_via_rlhf_f3ae188d` (2024-09-19; middle author) 
  > "We are limiting ourselves to the controlled, relatively unrealistic setting of unambiguous multiple-choice questions, and we are not examining the effects of any form of further fine-tuning based on the knowledge we elicit"  
  > -- `research__measuring_progress_on_scalable_oversight_for_large_b0f6f129` (2022-11-04; first author)
- Self-reports of eval suspicion as the main indicator. 
  > "More likely, and I think more often, models will, I think, be acting in a way that feels a little cartoonish, that feels like it's kind of playing along with the story without saying this overtly. That's this kind of subtle evidence we have to watch out for."  
  > -- `research__claude_finds_god_asterisk_d201cd5e` (2025-07-15; solo author)
